title: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)

sections.label: Patients with frequent clinic visits
sections.summary: Over 7,000 patients each had 24 or more clinic visits a year, and over 2,000 each had 36 or more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Over 7,000 patients each had 24 or more clinic visits a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Over 2,000 patients each with 36 or more clinic visits a year.

sections.label: Family doctors linking with hospitals
sections.summary: It asks whether family doctors can more easily link up with hospital teams to support patients in the community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can it be easier for family doctors to link up with the hospital team, to keep updated on the mutual patient's condition, or even to mobilise the resources of a hospital cluster, working with family doctors to help support patients in the community?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need to keep our healthcare system fit for purpose, amidst Singapore's ageing population.

sections.label: Public healthcare consultations in 2019
sections.summary: In 2019 there were 14 million public healthcare consultations, and one minute less per worker would save 14 million minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2019, the last year before COVID-19, from public available figures, there were 14 million consultations across the public healthcare sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Imagine: if healthcare workers spent just one minute less waiting in front of a computer, waiting for a computer app to load, working with a mouse, data entry, or grappling with technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: That alone, Mr Speaker, would mean 14 million minutes saved in the healthcare system; a quarter-million hours, 10,000 work days, or 27 years of someone working 24 hours a day – that is how much time could be saved.

sections.label: IP insurer doctor panels
sections.summary: Clementi residents asked why IP insurers' doctor panels differ, and MOH is called on to improve patients' journey.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some Clementi residents have asked: "Why are IP insurers’ panels of doctors so different from one company to another?" In May last year, the Singapore Medical Association (SMA) News reported that one IP insurer for their panel of breast surgeons only had male surgeons, which meant a female patient, if needing a female breast surgeon in the private sector would have to co-pay more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Unless the different insurers have made these decisions due to business considerations, rather than clinical performance – in which case, the insurers should be upfront and transparent with patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I call upon MOH to continue looking at this to see how we can make the journey better for patients who have invested many years of their CPF, MediSave savings or personal funds in IP Plans.

sections.label: Raising nurses and allied health pay
sections.summary: It says there is still room to look at raising remuneration of nurses and allied health workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, then Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat announced improvements, but there is still room to look further at raising the remuneration of our nurses and our allied health workers because what our nurses and allied health sisters and brothers do is essential work, deep skills, physical, mental, emotional labour, reducing the burden of suffering for patients and patients' families.

sections.label: Support for outsourced healthcare workers
sections.summary: It asks MOH for an update on what is being done to better support outsourced healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MOH provide an update on what is being done to better support our outsourced sisters and brothers in healthcare?

sections.label: Research on healthcare workers' performance
sections.summary: In 2007, in SMA News, the speaker asked whether more research was needed into how long shifts and sleep deprivation shape healthcare workers' performance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2007, 15 years ago, in SMA News, I asked whether we should do more research into how the performance of healthcare workers is shaped by long shifts and sleep deprivation.

sections.label: Family-friendly healthcare workplaces
sections.summary: The passage calls for making healthcare workplaces more family-friendly and inclusive for workers with diverse backgrounds and personal journeys.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Young doctors who worry if becoming a mother will have implications for their traineeship journey.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We must keep on looking at how to make our healthcare workplaces more family-friendly, because that is how we build more inclusive workplace for healthcare workers across a diversity of backgrounds, a diversity of personal journeys.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The lives of our loved ones, the life of every Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We owe it to our fellow Singaporeans to keep our healthcare system fit for purpose, not just for today, but for tomorrow.

sections.label: UK GP enrolment model
sections.summary: In the United Kingdom, more than 99% of residents are enrolled with GPs who provide health screening and follow-up care within six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the United Kingdom, more than 99% of residents are enrolled with their General Practitioners (GPs) who will provide health screening and follow-up care within six months of their enrolment.

sections.label: Resources for GP preventive care
sections.summary: The speaker asks if MOH will consider more resources and incentives to encourage GPs in preventive and chronic disease management for the ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to ask if MOH will consider providing more resources and incentives to encourage GPs to step up in preventive and chronic disease management to enhance healthcare for our ageing population?

sections.label: GP enrolment in primary care network
sections.summary: The speaker asks about the progress of GP enrolment in the primary care network, noting holistic senior healthcare goes beyond physical health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But holistic healthcare for seniors goes beyond physical health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I wish to ask on the progress of the enrolment of GPs in the primary care network.

sections.label: Gatekeeping model for specialist care
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a Nordic-style gatekeeping model for specialist care is intended, or whether the relationship is mainly for chronic disease management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Do we intend to introduce a similar model of gatekeeping to specialist care as in the Nordic countries, or do we intend for this relationship to be primarily for chronic disease management?

sections.label: Preventive healthcare spending and LumiHealth
sections.summary: About 5% of MOH's non-COVID-19 budget went to preventive healthcare, including $330 million for the Health Promotion Board and the LumiHealth e-voucher scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Ong Ye Kung during his recent event has already predicted that healthcare expenditure in Singapore will triple in the coming decade to almost $60 billion by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the last two years, about 5% of the MOH non-COVID-19-related budget was spent on preventive healthcare efforts, including the $330 million to fund the work of the Health Promotion Board (HPB).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Spending 5% of the healthcare budget on preventive healthcare is quite respectable, as compared to 2.9% in US and 5.9% in Canada.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, the scheme to give up to $380 worth of e-vouchers when one uses the LumiHealth app for the Apple Watch to achieve healthy lifestyle goals.

sections.label: MOH war on sugar
sections.summary: In 2016, MOH declared a war against sugar and set up a new task force chaired by then Minister Gan Kim Yong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2016, MOH declared a war against sugar and set up a new task force, chaired by then Minister Gan Kim Yong.

sections.label: Medical subsidies and rising healthcare expenditure
sections.summary: The Government introduced medical subsidy schemes, and healthcare expenditure tripled to $11.3 billion in 2019 and is expected to hit $27 billion by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The Government has swiftly addressed some of these concerns over the years by introducing various medical subsidy schemes, including Pioneer Generation, Merdeka Generation health benefits, CHAS cards for middle and lower-income groups to cushion the impact of rising healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Healthcare expenditure has tripled to $11.3 billion in 2019, from $3.7 billion in 2010, over a 10-year period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: And with the current spending in this sector, excluding COVID-19 related expenditure, it is expected to rise and hit $27 billion by 2030, which means that in another decade, it will triple again.

sections.label: GST hike to fund healthcare
sections.summary: The Government gave funding expected healthcare increases due to the ageing population as a reason for the GST hike in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: In this Budget, one of the reasons given by the Government for the GST hike is to fund the expected increase in healthcare due to the ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: How will the Government use the increase in revenue collected through the GST hike to improve healthcare delivery to our ageing population?

sections.label: Nurse to population ratio
sections.summary: Singapore's nurse to population ratio is around 7.5 nurses per 1,000 population, lower than the OECD average of nine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At around 7.5 nurses to 1,000 population, our nurse to population ratio is lower than the OECD average of nine.

sections.label: UK Health and Care Worker Visa
sections.summary: The UK's Health and Care Worker Visa allows settlement after five years and lets applicants be joined by dependent partners and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The UK has launched the Health and Care Worker Visa that allows settlement in the UK after five years and applicants can be joined by dependent partners and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What more is the Government doing to attract, train and retain nurses?

sections.label: Recruiting diverse leadership and COVID measures
sections.summary: The passage asks about recruiting and deploying people from different backgrounds into leadership and notes countries removing COVID-19 measures while cases remain high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what is being done to recruit, nurture and deploy people from different backgrounds, especially in leadership roles?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Chairman, it has been several years since we embarked on the "3 Beyonds" strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: But I have a lot of hope that we are now ready to make some bold calls to really unlock it and move forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, since the end of last year, many countries around the world have removed most, if not, all of the COVID-19-differentiation measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With the infection cases and deaths from COVID-19 still at a high level, we are not against postponing the easing of the slew of COVID-19 measures announced by Minister Ong Ye Kung on 16 February.

sections.label: HSA vaccine safety update
sections.summary: HSA's 23 February update reported 10 serious and 280 non-serious side effect cases in children aged five to 11 after vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The latest vaccine safety update by HSA on 23 February reported 10 cases of children, aged five to 11, with serious side effects following vaccination and 280 cases of non-serious side effects.

sections.label: Omicron surge and VDS
sections.summary: The passage states that Omicron infections continue to surge despite all VDS being in place, indicating VDS are not critical against the virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With the continuous surge in Omicron infections despite having all the VDS in place indicates that the VDS are not critical in the fight against the virus anymore.

sections.label: Therapeutics for senior patients
sections.summary: The passage asks whether approved therapeutics like Molnupiravir or Paxlovid should be available to senior patients through GPs before hospitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Should approved therapeutics like Molnupiravir or Paxlovid not be made available to senior patients through the GPs, even before they turn seriously ill and need hospitalisation?

sections.label: Concierge contracts and referral fees
sections.summary: The passage states doctors on such contracts pay referral fees and are asked to restrict referrals, limiting patient choice and autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I do not have any access to contracts and only a few colleagues have told me in confidence about how these work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such services may be marketed as free for patients, but doctors have to pay a referral fee, which may be a percentage of their usual professional fees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, it is said that doctors on such contracts are asked to restrict referrals to other doctors on such concierge contracts, thereby restricting patient choice, which is against the concept of patient autonomy.

sections.label: Consultation fees and NDAs
sections.summary: The passage states some claim consultation fees may be as low as $6 but are bound by NDAs, so more information is unavailable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Several have claimed consultation fees may be as low as $6, but they are bound by NDAs, so I do not have more information.

sections.label: Delayed payments and cash flow
sections.summary: Payments may be delayed up to six months, causing cash flow problems for a small practice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Payments may be delayed for as long as six months, causing cash flow problems for a small practice.

sections.label: Manpower Minister on EB plans
sections.summary: Dr Tan See Leng replied favourably on increased worker education on EB versus IP plans and a relook at TPA and EB plan administration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In reply to a supplementary question I asked in August last year, Minister for Manpower Dr Tan See Leng replied favourably that there can be increased education to workers on the use of EB versus IP plans, a relook at how TPAs and EB plans are administered, with a need for multiple stakeholders to be involved.

sections.label: Transition to COVID-19 endemicity
sections.summary: In late June 2021, the Multi-Ministry Task Force announced plans to transition to COVID-19 endemicity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In late June 2021, the Multi-Ministry Task Force (MTF) announced plans to transition to COVID-19 endemicity.

sections.label: Healthcare worker resignations reported
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Janil reported about 1,500 healthcare workers resigned in the first half of 2021, compared to about 2,000 annually pre-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In November 2021, Senior Minister of State Janil reported to the House that about 1,500 healthcare workers had resigned in the first half of 2021, compared to about 2,000 annually pre-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Close to 500 doctors and nurses, healthcare workers, resigned in the first half of 2021 as compared to around 500 in the whole of 2020 and around 600 in 2019, about double the usual rate.

sections.label: Public hospital manning situation
sections.summary: The passage asks what the manning situation in public hospitals is as a percentage today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a percentage today, what is the manning situation in our public hospitals?

sections.label: Sleep deprivation and psycho-motor abilities
sections.summary: Sleep deprivation research shows it can impair psycho-motor abilities to a degree comparable to intoxication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Sleep deprivation research shows it can impair psycho-motor abilities to a degree comparable to intoxication.

sections.label: Abuse cases and worker resignations
sections.summary: Abuse or harassment cases rose from 1,200 in 2019 to 1,400 by end-November last year, and 1,500 workers resigned in the first half of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The number of abuse or harassment cases rose from 1,200 in 2019 to 1,400 as at the end of November last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2021, 1,500 workers resigned, compared with 2,000 annually before the pandemic.

sections.label: Ministerial Statement on healthcare resignations
sections.summary: A November 2021 Ministerial Statement showed worrying resignation rates, with foreign healthcare workers resigning in bigger numbers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Ministerial Statement in November 2021 showed worrying resignation rates with foreign healthcare workers resigning in bigger numbers.

sections.label: Medical resident burnout and manpower planning
sections.summary: A 2017 local study found eight in 10 medical residents burnt out, and asked what will change in healthcare manpower planning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A local study by NUS Medicine, National Heart Centre Singapore and Duke-NUS Medical School in 2017 found that eight out of 10 medical residents were burnt out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Taking into consideration the ageing population and the threat of Pandemic X, what will change moving forward, with the master planning of manpower capacity for the healthcare sector so we can take into account the working environment and wellness of the healthcare workers?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This may mean, among other things, beyond remuneration, better work-life balance, enough manpower for better working hours, the ability to take sufficient leave instead of encashing them and the improvement of the healthcare worker to patient ratio.

sections.label: Rising reported harassment cases
sections.summary: The number of harassment cases reported has been increasing yearly, from 1,080 to 1,300 cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: The number of harassment cases reported has been increasing yearly, from 1,080 to 1,300 cases.

sections.label: Public healthcare workers under POHA
sections.summary: Healthcare professionals in public healthcare institutions are categorised as Public Service Workers under the Protection from Harassment Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: Healthcare professionals in public healthcare institutions are categorised as Public Service Workers under the Protection from Harassment Act.

sections.label: POHA coverage and remedies
sections.summary: The Protection from Harassment Act covers only public healthcare workers and does not allow immediate remedies to be taken.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: The Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) covers only public healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: It does not allow for immediate remedies to be taken.

sections.label: Caring society and healthcare worker abuse
sections.summary: The passage supports building a more caring and inclusive society and welcomes MOH's zero-tolerance stance against abuse and harassment of healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: As Minister Lawrence Wong said, let us build a more caring and inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: I applaud MOH’s written response on 10 January that states a zero-tolerance stance towards the abuse and harassment of healthcare workers.

sections.label: Protecting healthcare workers and support
sections.summary: The passage suggests stronger legislation to protect healthcare workers, notes public support, and cites MOH's monetary award of up to $4,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: Maybe COVID-19 has, indeed, made it timely for there to be stronger legislation to protect all healthcare workers against bullying and harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are also heartened to see many individuals and organisations that have stepped forward to lend support with food, care packs and others to show our appreciation to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It was very heartening that on 5 November 2021, MOH boosted the public healthcare workers with an announcement of a monetary award of up to $4,000 in recognition of their efforts in the fight against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, this applies to those at community care organisations that deliver frontline services, such as nursing homes and dialysis centres.

sections.label: Bonus appeal for healthcare workers
sections.summary: The passage appeals to the Minister for Health to give a one-off bonus to more healthcare workers, including outsourced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: News of these resignations from this group of healthcare workers should not be seen as an obstacle for fellow Singaporeans or even students who may want to pursue a career in healthcare – friends and cousins that I know of are still contemplating their decision in this meaningful sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am appealing to the Government, specifically to the Minister for Health, to again give out one-off bonus for this group of workers, not just confining to the earlier groups that had benefited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, there are also outsourced workers, such as cleaners, housekeepers, porters, technicians and even security officers, whose lives are equally exposed in hospitals, community care organisations and also neighbourhood clinics.

sections.label: Support for mothers and families
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry for updates from the Mental Health and Well-being Taskforce and the Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Taskforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Support programmes and resources for mothers and families as a whole must continue to be made available and accessible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Ministry what are the updates from the Mental Health and Well-being Taskforce as well as the Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Taskforce respectively.

sections.label: Interagency mental health taskforce progress
sections.summary: The passage states that an Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being was set up on 23 August 2021 and asks for a progress update.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: On 23 August 2021, an Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being was set up to address the multifactorial nature of mental health and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: Could the Minister update on the progress of works since the announcement?

sections.label: Permanent mental health office question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a permanent office or agency would be more effective and what factors are considered for forming one under PMO.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: The mental well-being of a nation is essential for Singaporeans to reach their full potential.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: Therefore, would it be more effective to make it a permanent office or agency?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: Since it also requires close coordination among many Ministries such as SNDGO, could the Ministry share what factors it considers when determining whether to form a permanent office under PMO, to oversee an issue of national concern?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: An IMH study last year found that 13% of the participants reported symptoms of increased anxiety and depression.

sections.label: MediSave limits for mental conditions
sections.summary: Patients with complex chronic mental conditions can use up to $700 of MediSave yearly, while other patients can use up to $500 yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Patients with complex chronic mental conditions will be able to use up to $700 of Medisave per patient yearly, while other patients will be able to use up to $500 of their MediSave per patient yearly for treatments.

sections.label: MediSave for psychologist consultations
sections.summary: The speaker asks that MediSave payments be allowed for consultation with a psychologist, which is currently not possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Further, as part of the new focus on mental wellness, I would like to ask that we allow MediSave payments for consultation with psychologist, which I understand it is currently not possible.

sections.label: NKF dialysis centre applications
sections.summary: According to NKF, dialysis centres are receiving more than 100 applications a month, up from 60 a few years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, according to NKF, dialysis centres are experiencing a growing number of applications, more than 100 a month, up from 60 a few years ago.

sections.label: Peritoneal dialysis and nurse manpower
sections.summary: Peritoneal dialysis can help tackle a manpower crunch because it requires half the nurses needed for hemodialysis with the same number of patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Peritoneal dialysis can also help tackle a manpower crunch faced as the number of nurses required are halved, compared to the nurses needed for hemodialysis with the same number of patients.

sections.label: Smart technology and telehealth adoption
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry plans to use smart technology to relieve the healthcare crunch and accelerate telehealth adoption in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: How does the Ministry plan to use smart technology to relieve the healthcare crunch?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Within the community, how can we accelerate the adoption of telehealth?

sections.label: Healthcare data and IT security
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry is doing to ensure security of healthcare data and IT systems and how lessons from the 2018 SingHealth hack are applied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: What is the Ministry doing to ensure security of our data and IT systems in the healthcare sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: How are we applying the lessons learnt from the 2018 SingHealth hack and subsequent cybersecurity breaches in other healthcare systems?

sections.label: Ageing Plan Refresh update
sections.summary: The speaker says an update on the Ageing Plan Refresh is urgently needed as the pandemic ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: As we emerge from the pandemic, we urgently need an update on the Ageing Plan Refresh.

sections.label: Careline senior support service
sections.summary: MOH rolled out Careline in 2016, and the Minister for Health said it has supported around 10,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In 2016, MOH rolled out the senior support call centre service, Careline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Minister for Health last year noted that Careline has supported around 10,000 seniors.

sections.label: Careline calls referred to emergency services
sections.summary: The question asks how many Careline calls in 2019, 2020 and 2021 were referred to emergency services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: How many Careline calls in 2019, 2020 and 2021 have been referred to emergency services?

sections.label: MOH Ageing Plan Refresh review
sections.summary: The speaker notes MOH has started the Ageing Plan Refresh to review whole-of-Government efforts to empower and support seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Chairman, I noted that MOH has stared on the Ageing Plan Refresh, which gives the Government an opportunity to review the whole-of-Government efforts to empower and support our seniors, which is much needed given how much change has happened with COVID-19.

sections.label: Resuming seniors' community engagements safely
sections.summary: The question asks what the Government is doing to resume seniors' engagements in the community safely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: What is the Government doing to resume seniors' engagements in the community in a safe manner?

sections.label: Seniors aged 65 and above
sections.summary: Population in Brief 2021 reports a rising share of citizens aged 65 and above, with 22.8% living alone or with spouse only.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Population in Brief 2021 continues to report an increasing trend of our citizen population aged 65 and above, with the proportion growing at a faster pace compared to the last decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: From Census 2020 data, we note that 22.8% of this group of seniors are living alone or with their spouse only.

sections.label: Children's Internet usage rise
sections.summary: IMDA data shows Internet usage among children aged 15 and below rose from 69% in 2016 to 92% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: According to data from IMDA, Internet usage among children aged 15 and below increased from 69% in 2016 to 92% in 2020.

sections.label: Screen time addiction cases
sections.summary: A Straits Times informal study in February with counselling agencies showed screen time addiction intervention cases rose up to 60% during the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: An informal study done by The Straits Times in February this year with several counselling agencies showed that the number of cases they received for intervention regarding screen time addiction rose by up to 60% during the circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Singapore low fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore has been experiencing a low Total Fertility Rate.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Singapore has been experiencing low Total Fertility Rate (TFR).

sections.label: Chronic diseases and healthcare costs
sections.summary: A study of a polyclinic cluster showed median annual per capita healthcare costs increase with the number of chronic diseases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: A study on a cluster of polyclinics in Singapore has shown that the median annual healthcare costs per capita increase with the number of chronic diseases.

sections.label: Technology for chronic disease care
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOH will consider more technology, including telehealth and artificial intelligence, and asks how it will leverage technology and make care affordable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: In this regard, I hope that MOH will consider more use of technology, including telehealth and artificial intelligence amidst our nation's digitalisation efforts to help individuals monitor and manage our health in partnership with our healthcare providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: I hope to ask MOH how it will leverage on technology amongst our healthcare professionals and patients, especially in the space of prevention and management of chronic diseases and how it will help to make care treatment augmented by technologies, such as telehealth affordable through, for example, the use of MediSave or CHAS.

sections.label: National Adult Immunisation Schedule
sections.summary: The National Adult Immunisation Schedule was set up in 2017 to guide vaccinations for those aged 18 and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS) was set up in 2017 to provide guidance on vaccinations that anyone aged 18 and above should adopt to protect themselves against vaccine-preventable diseases.

sections.label: Vaccination reminders and incentives
sections.summary: MOH is asked to consider reminders for missed vaccinations and incentives such as MediSave top-ups for updated vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Perhaps MOH can consider sending reminders to Singaporeans who have missed their scheduled vaccinations and also provide some incentives, such as MediSave top-ups for those who have their vaccinations updated?

sections.label: Unvaccinated share of ICU cases
sections.summary: Three percent of adults not fully vaccinated accounted for 25% of ICU cases and deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Three percent of our adult population who are not fully vaccinated accounted for 25% of our ICU cases and deaths.

sections.label: Risks for under-12s
sections.summary: For under-12s, about 40 per million severe adverse reactions follow vaccination, while infection risks include MIS-C and myocarditis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For individuals below the age of 12, there are about 40 per million severe adverse reactions reported after vaccination and most of these will recover quite quickly with no effects, no long-term effects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: When an individual under 12 is infected by COVID-19, the risk is that about 320 individuals per million will develop Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) and about 450 per million will develop myocarditis.

sections.label: Boosted individuals less likely to die
sections.summary: Hospitalised vaccinated individuals with booster doses are 33 times less likely to die from COVID-19 than those not fully vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: At the other end, if you are admitted to hospital, vaccinated individuals who have received their booster doses are 33 times less likely to die from COVID-19, as compared to individuals who are not fully vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, to Mr Leong – it is not appropriate to lift the measures at this stage.

sections.label: Mental health taskforce focus areas
sections.summary: The Taskforce identified four focus areas covering family support, mental health care access, employment support and mental health literacy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Taskforce has identified four focus areas: first, to strengthen services and family support for parents and youths; second, to provide and improve access to quality and affordable mental health care by integrating health and social services; third, to provide employment support for persons with mental health conditions; and fourth, to improve mental health literacy among the citizens and create an inclusive society for persons with mental health conditions.

sections.label: Network individuals and initiatives
sections.summary: The Network brought together more than 1,500 individuals and saw over 20 ground-up initiatives formed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Network has brought together more than 1,500 individuals and saw the formation of over 20 ground-up initiatives.

sections.label: Psychiatric services at Alexandra Hospital
sections.summary: The National University Health System will set up psychiatric services at the redeveloped Alexandra Hospital alongside general hospital services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The National University Health System will set up psychiatric services at the redeveloped Alexandra Hospital, in addition to the general hospital services that would be located there.

sections.label: Youth mental health outreach teams
sections.summary: Youth community outreach teams and youth integrated teams support persons aged 12 to 25 at risk of mental health conditions, with four outreach and two integrated teams rolled out in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have piloted youth community outreach teams and youth integrated teams to provide a range of support to persons aged 12 to 25 who are at risk, or who are suspected to have mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have rolled out four outreach teams and two youth integrated teams in 2021.

sections.label: MediSave for mental health conditions
sections.summary: Patients can use the MediSave500/700 scheme to pay for treatments for four mental health conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Patients can tap on the MediSave500/700 scheme to pay for treatments for four mental health conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP).

sections.label: Mobile Inpatient Care at Home sandbox
sections.summary: Initial success of these programmes prompted a study on extending them to other hospitalised patients and clinical services under a Mobile Inpatient Care at Home sandbox.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The initial success of these programmes and services has prompted us to study how we can extend it to other groups of hospitalised patients and more clinical services under a Mobile Inpatient Care at Home (MIC@Home) sandbox.

sections.label: Home blood pressure monitoring in polyclinics
sections.summary: Patients monitor blood pressure at home and submit readings to a polyclinic care team via a Bluetooth machine and mobile application, saving a polyclinic visit; this will scale to all polyclinics and other conditions such as diabetes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: These patients monitor their blood pressure regularly at home and submit their readings to a care team in the polyclinic, through a Bluetooth-enabled blood pressure machine and a mobile phone application, saving them a visit to the polyclinic while still receiving timely support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will be scaling this to all polyclinics and progressively introduce the approach to other conditions such as diabetes.

sections.label: Digital drawing test for dementia
sections.summary: An interagency team used local clinical and technology expertise to develop a digital drawing test that takes as little as 10 minutes to estimate dementia risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: By using local clinical and technology expertise, an interagency team has developed a digital drawing test, draw with a pen or stylus on a tablet.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It takes as little as 10 minutes to estimate the risk of dementia.

sections.label: New polyclinics and nursing homes
sections.summary: Last year, three new polyclinics and five new nursing homes opened, including NTUC Health (Tampines) Nursing Home, a CTF since September 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Last year, we opened three new polyclinics and five new nursing homes including the new NTUC Health (Tampines) Nursing Home which has operated as a Community Treatment Facility (CTF) since September 2021 to support our fight against COVID-19.

sections.label: Taman Jurong polyclinic by 2028
sections.summary: Under the plan to expand to 32 polyclinics by 2030, Taman Jurong residents can expect a new polyclinic by 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As part of our plan to expand to 32 polyclinics by 2030, residents of Taman Jurong can look forward to a new polyclinic by 2028.

sections.label: MOH details and thanks to workers
sections.summary: MOH colleagues will provide plan details in further speeches, and the speaker records thanks to all healthcare workers for their service to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Details about our plans from MOH will be provided in the further speeches by my MOH colleagues, but I would like to record my thanks to all healthcare workers for their service to Singapore.

sections.label: Tools for healthcare workers
sections.summary: The speech highlighted examples of ensuring healthcare workers have the best tools, technology, services and infrastructure to deliver the best possible care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In my speech, I have highlighted examples through which we will make sure that our healthcare workers will have the best possible tools, technology, services and infrastructure, so that they can focus on delivering the best possible care.

sections.label: ICU surge equipment and trained nurses
sections.summary: There is sufficient equipment and consumables to step up ICU beds significantly, and over 800 non-ICU nurses were trained as a reserve by January 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To Mr Pritam Singh’s query about preparations for ICU surges, I want to reassure him that we have sufficient equipment and consumables to step up ICU beds significantly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And as of January 2022, more than 800 non-ICU nurses have been trained as a reserve to augment ICU nursing manpower by up to 57%.

sections.label: Public healthcare workforce size
sections.summary: As of end 2021, the public healthcare workforce was about 62,500 staff, an increase of about 1,800 from end 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As of end 2021, the public healthcare workforce stood at about 62,500 staff, an increase of about 1,800 compared to end 2020.

sections.label: Nurse attrition rates comparison
sections.summary: The two-year average was similar to 2019 levels, but 2021 attrition was 14.8% for foreign nurses versus 7.4% for local nurses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: So, the two-year average was quite similar to 2019 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: However, the 2021 attrition among foreign nurses was 14.8%, much higher than the 7.4% among local nurses.

sections.label: Healthcare programme intake increases
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2021, medicine and nursing intakes each rose about 15%, while allied health combined intake rose about 65%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2021, intakes for medicine and nursing each increased by about 15%, while the combined intake for allied health programmes increased by about 65%.

sections.label: MOH staff well-being measures
sections.summary: MOH is reviewing staff feedback, well-being and mental health tracking, plans Wellness Officers in every cluster, and is reviewing staffing norms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOH is working with the clusters to review and improve staff feedback channels, staff well-being and mental health tracking and monitoring processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: There are also plans to appoint a Wellness Officer or its equivalent in every cluster to oversee and develop the system changes that are needed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We are also reviewing our staffing norms in the public healthcare system to strengthen our resilience to future shocks and better cope with fluctuations in workload.

sections.label: Junior doctors' work hours
sections.summary: Singapore Medical Council guidelines allow junior doctors up to 80 hours weekly, and surveys showed 20% exceeded this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Singapore Medical Council guidelines stipulate that junior doctors may work up to 80 hours a week, including overnight duties of not more than 24 hours, with up to six hours after that for handover or training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Surveys showed that 20% of all junior doctors exceeded the stipulated 80-hour work week.

sections.label: Restarting trials
sections.summary: When the situation allows, there is intent to restart the trials.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: When the situation allows, we intend to restart the trials.

sections.label: National Wellness Committee formed
sections.summary: MOH has formed the National Wellness Committee for Junior Doctors as a first step.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that many of them recognised the complexity and inter-linked nature of the issues pertaining to junior doctors’ working hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Therefore, as a first step, MOH has formed the National Wellness Committee for Junior Doctors.

sections.label: Preliminary and final recommendations timeline
sections.summary: The workgroup aims to put forth preliminary recommendations by the middle of this year and complete final recommendations by early 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The issues are complex and seeks to change years of established practice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We aim to put forth preliminary recommendations by the middle of this year so that some immediate measures can be implemented, with a view to completing their final recommendations by early 2023.

sections.label: Rise in such cases
sections.summary: At end 2021, there were about 1,500 such cases, up from 1,080 cases in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: At end 2021, there were about 1,500 such cases, up from 1,080 cases in 2018.

sections.label: Zero-tolerance approach to abuse
sections.summary: MOH and public healthcare institutions adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards abuse and harassment of healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOH and our public healthcare institutions adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards abuse and harassment of our healthcare workers.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup for Prevention
sections.summary: MOH will establish the Tripartite Workgroup for the Prevention of Abuse and Harassment of Healthcare Workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOH will, therefore, be establishing the Tripartite Workgroup for the Prevention of Abuse and Harassment of Healthcare Workers.

sections.label: Chronic Disease Management Programme expansion
sections.summary: From 1 July this year, chronic conditions in the Chronic Disease Management Programme will expand from 20 to 23, benefiting more than 134,000 individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On healthcare affordability, Dr Tan Wu Meng will be happy to know that from 1 July this year, we will expand the number of chronic conditions in the Chronic Disease Management Programme from 20 to 23.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The three new conditions included allergic rhinitis, gout and chronic hepatitis B.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: More than 134,000 individuals will benefit as they can now use their MediSave and CHAS subsidies for these conditions.

sections.label: Integrated Shield Plan panel expansion
sections.summary: Most IP insurers have at least 500 private specialists, with each insurer's panel covering 80% to 90% of their private medical institution claims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On Dr Tan Wu Meng's concerns on Integrated Panels, we had earlier announced that Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurers had accepted the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee's (MHIC) recommendation to expand their panels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Today, most IP insurers have at least 500 private specialists, with each insurer's panel covering 80% to 90% of their private medical institution claims.

sections.label: Interagency task force child maternal health
sections.summary: An interagency task force was set up last year to develop a five-year Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Last year, we set up the interagency task force to develop a five-year Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Strategy.

sections.label: Mother-child dyad service pilots
sections.summary: Two mother-child dyad service pilots began at Punggol and Yishun polyclinics, benefiting more than 10,000 children and mothers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To this end, we started two mother-child dyad service pilots at our polyclinics – the Integrated Maternal and Child Wellness Hub programme at Punggol Polyclinic since 2019 and the EMBRACE programme at Yishun polyclinic in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since their launch, I am glad that more than 10,000 children and mothers have benefited from these services.

sections.label: Scaling up mother-child dyad services
sections.summary: MOH will scale up mother-child dyad services to 12 more polyclinics over three years, and EMBRACEPLUS was rolled out.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are happy with the success of the pilots and the positive feedback given by the parents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am pleased to announce that MOH will scale up the mother-child dyad services to 12 more polyclinics over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To strengthen support for children with higher or more complex needs, the National Healthcare Group Polyclinics has also rolled out the EMBRACEPLUS programme, a component of EMBRACE pilot.

sections.label: Integrated family support programme pilot
sections.summary: An integrated family support programme will be piloted later this year at a one-stop community node with a concierge service representative.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To this end, I am glad to share that we will pilot an integrated family support programme later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Families can access varied services at a one-stop community node near their homes, such as polyclinic, a GP clinic or a social service agency.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For example, families can attend both parent support groups organised by Families for Life @ Community and receive vaccinations or developmental screening for their children at the same location.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will also have a "concierge service" representative onsite.

sections.label: Reducing multiple site visits
sections.summary: The pilot will reduce families' need to visit multiple sites and integrate wraparound support across social-health domains.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The pilot will reduce the need for families to visit multiple sites for different services and most importantly, to integrate and provide wraparound support across the social-health domains for families as their children grow.

sections.label: Diabetes prevalence and Nutri-Grade labelling
sections.summary: Diabetes prevalence stayed stable at 7.9% from 2017 to 2020, and Nutri-Grade beverages face new labelling and advertising rules from 30 December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since then, based on the recent National Population Health Survey, age-standardised prevalence of diabetes has remained stable at 7.9% from 2017 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: From 30 December 2022, Nutri-Grade beverages sold in Singapore in prepacked form and from automatic beverage dispensers will be subject to new labelling requirements and advertising prohibitions.

sections.label: Healthier choice beverage market share
sections.summary: From 2017 to 2019, healthier choice beverages rose from 58.6% to 71.7% of the market and median sugar level fell from 8.5% to 6.3%.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: From when engagement started with the industry in 2017 to 2019, the proportion of healthier choice beverages in the market increased from 58.6% to 71.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The median sugar level of sweetened beverages has also decreased from 8.5% to 6.3% over the same period.

sections.label: Singapore residents sodium consumption
sections.summary: Singapore residents consume an average of 3.6 grammes of sodium a day.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Singapore residents are on average consuming 3.6 grammes of sodium a day.

sections.label: Measures against vaping
sections.summary: HPB and the Health Sciences Authority are using multi-pronged measures against vaping, and HPB plans a vape-free campaign in 2022 for youths and younger adults.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Together with HPB and the Health Sciences Authority, we are employing heightened multi-pronged measures against vaping.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To strengthen public education efforts and reduce demand for vaping, HPB is planning to roll out a vape-free campaign later in 2022 targeted at youths and younger adults through popular digital platforms.

sections.label: Influenza vaccination uptake and subsidies
sections.summary: Influenza vaccination uptake in persons aged 65 to 74 rose from 14% in 2017 to 23% in 2020, and subsidies were extended since November 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Based on the National Population Health Survey 2020, the uptake for influenza vaccination in persons aged 65 to 74 has increased from 14% in 2017 to 23% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To make vaccinations recommended under the NAIS more affordable and accessible, subsidies have been extended to these vaccinations since November 2020, at both CHAS GP clinics and polyclinics.

sections.label: Pilot programme satisfaction and habits
sections.summary: Preliminary pilot results show more than 90% were satisfied and about one-third adopted healthier habits in nutrition, mental well-being and physical activity.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Preliminary results from the pilot indicate that more than 90% were satisfied with the programme and about one-third of them have started to adopt healthier habits in the areas of nutrition, mental well-being and physical activity.

sections.label: Our Healthy Singapore Fund
sections.summary: HPB is partnering MCCY to establish a $1.5 million Our Healthy Singapore Fund supporting community volunteers and partners to develop programmes for a healthier nation.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: HPB is partnering MCCY to establish a $1.5 million Our Healthy Singapore Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The fund will support more community volunteers and partners like Mr Azrin and Mdm Lalitha to develop programmes that are closely in tune with their communities’ needs, and therefore, be more targeted and effective in developing a healthier nation.

sections.label: Women's Health Committee event
sections.summary: The Women's Health Committee the speaker chairs will run a women's health event later in the year to amplify awareness and create sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To amplify awareness and create sustainability to some of these initiatives, the Women’s Health Committee that I chair will run a women’s health event in the later part of the year.

sections.label: Action Plan for Successful Ageing refresh
sections.summary: Over 5,000 Singaporeans were engaged to discuss refreshing the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, with plans on Care, Contribution and Connectedness.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the Ageing Plan refresh.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have engaged over 5,000 Singaporeans from all walks of life to discuss the refresh of our Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Over the past year, we also started working on our plans to support seniors in the three Cs: Care, Contribution and Connectedness.

sections.label: Eldercare Centres by June 2022
sections.summary: By June 2022, over 115 Eldercare Centres will be set up.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: By June 2022, we will set up over 115 Eldercare Centres.

sections.label: Seniors programme, palliative care, housing-cum-care
sections.summary: A holistic programme to empower seniors' well-being rolls out nationwide from May 2022, with home palliative places grown and a private Government Land Sale in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Through a holistic programme, it aims to empower seniors to improve and maintain their physical, mental and social well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It will be gradually rolled out nationwide from May 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For example, as Mr Yip Hon Weng pointed out, palliative care is an important focus.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have grown our home palliative places steadily from 2,900 places in 2019 to 3,400 places in 2021 to fulfil seniors’ wishes to pass on at home.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Last year, we also launched the Community Care Apartments at Bukit Batok, which was oversubscribed.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We, therefore, see potential in expanding the housing-cum-care model to the private sector.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As announced by MND, we will launch a private Government Land Sale in 2022 to catalyse care innovation for seniors, where tenderers will be invited to propose innovative assisted living models.

sections.label: Preventive care healthcare initiative update
sections.summary: The speaker updates Members on a major healthcare initiative focusing on preventive care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, today, I would like to update Members on a major healthcare initiative to focus on preventive care.

sections.label: Growth in hospital beds, doctors, nurses
sections.summary: Acute hospital beds increased by 40% with three new acute public hospitals, doctors and specialists rose 65% to almost 15,000, and nurses rose 45% to 42,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Let us take acute hospital beds which increased by 40%, as we opened three new acute public hospitals – Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, Sengkang General Hospital, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The number of doctors and specialists increased by 65% to almost 15,000 now; nurses increased by 45% to 42,000 now.

sections.label: One in five by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, that number goes to one in five.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By 2030, that number goes to one in five.

sections.label: Obesity rate rise 2017-2020
sections.summary: From 2017 to 2020, the obesity rate rose from under 9% to over 10%, undoing years of progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From 2017 to 2020, the obesity rate has gone up from under 9% to over 10%, undoing many years of progress.

sections.label: Healthcare costs and GST increase
sections.summary: Rising healthcare expenditure, projected to reach $27 billion in 2030, is the key reason additional GST revenue is needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Beyond the immediate family, sickness across the population imposes a huge burden on the healthcare system and on our taxpayers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We heard this sobering piece of data during the Budget debate and Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned – Government healthcare expenditure tripled over the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Based on current trajectory, it will again, more or less triple in the next 10 years, to $27 billion in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By then, healthcare budget may well be larger than that for defence and education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To make healthcare affordable, the Government will have to continue to subsidise healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And that is the key reason why additional revenue from GST increases is needed.

sections.label: Healthier SG primary care strategy
sections.summary: A new primary care strategy called Healthier SG will be consulted on, then detailed in a White Paper for debate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Family doctors must then become the most important anchor of our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This new strategy centred around primary care is called Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Over the next few months, we will be consulting different stakeholders, Singaporeans from all walks of life, GPs, healthcare workers and community partners to gather their inputs and views.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOH will then flesh out the details in a White Paper and table it in this House for debate.

sections.label: Coordinating physician and regular doctors
sections.summary: Only three in five Singaporeans have a regular family doctor, who can be a coordinating physician.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They can be what Dr Tan Wu Meng described as the "coordinating physician".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: However, only three in five Singaporeans have a regular family doctor.

sections.label: Regular preventive care with family doctor
sections.summary: Seeing a family doctor for preventive care means regular scheduled check-ins at least once a year for screenings, tracking and advice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Seeing our family doctor for preventive care is different from the occasional visit to their clinics when we do not feel well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It means regular scheduled check-ins – at least once a year – so that the family doctor can assess your overall health condition, conduct necessary health screenings, track your results, administer vaccinations if need be, advise you on adjustments in lifestyles to help you achieve your health goals.

sections.label: Healthier SG resident commitment
sections.summary: Enrolling on Healthier SG commits a resident to see one family doctor and adopt one care plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By enrolling on Healthier SG, a resident will commit to see one family doctor and adopt one care plan.

sections.label: Regional reach to residents
sections.summary: Each region covers up to about 1.5 million residents, working with family doctors and partners, likely starting with people in their 40s and older.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Each will look after a region of up to about 1.5 million residents and work with the family doctors and other partners in the region to reach out to as many residents as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will probably start with people in their 40s and older, because that is when chronic illnesses may start to set in.

sections.label: Primary and community care share
sections.summary: A fifth of doctors and nurses are in primary and community care today, and by 2030 this must increase to at least a quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, a fifth of doctors and nurses are in primary and community care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By 2030, we will need to increase this to at least a quarter.

sections.label: Capitation funding for healthcare clusters
sections.summary: Funding for healthcare clusters will change from workload-based to a capitation model with a pre-determined fee per resident in the region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have been funding our healthcare clusters, largely by their workload, such as the number of treatments, number of surgeries and operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will change this to a capitation model, where healthcare clusters get a pre-determined fee for every resident living in the region that they are looking after.

sections.label: Healthier SG preventive health strategy
sections.summary: With an ageing population, the Healthier SG national strategy will focus on preventive health, providing health check-ins and improving lifestyle and habits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But with an ageing population, we need to recalibrate and tilt the balance towards preventive healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, we are going to launch the Healthier SG strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is a national strategy that focus on preventive health – a strategy that will provide health check-ins for Singaporeans and improve their lifestyle and habits.

sections.label: MOH public consultation on package
sections.summary: Over the next few months, MOH will conduct public consultation to gather views and inputs and come up with an attractive and affordable package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Over the next few months, MOH will conduct public consultation to gather views and inputs and come up with an attractive and affordable package.

sections.label: Healthier SG White Paper drafting
sections.summary: A Healthier SG White Paper will be drafted and tabled in Parliament for debate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: After designing the package, we will draft a Healthier SG White Paper and table it in Parliament for debate.

sections.label: S+3M healthcare safety net
sections.summary: Patients who cannot afford costs can apply for MediFund, continuing the S+3M multi-layered safety net.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And if there is still a small sum that the patient cannot afford, he can apply for MediFund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, subsidy, then MediShield, MediSave and MediFund – that is, essentially, the S+3M framework – a multi-layered safety net for healthcare and it will continue.

sections.label: Universal healthcare expanding to preventive care
sections.summary: The S+3M safety net stays universal and expands to preventive care and population health, with a fuller Healthier SG debate later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our multi-layered safety net in healthcare, embodied in the S+3M policy, will always be universal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is, we will not have a situation which happens in other countries, where a patient comes to a hospital and gets turned away because he is unable to pay, because he is not covered by insurance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That universality will now expand in coverage, beyond medical treatment, to preventive care and population health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The more well-off and better-informed are already taking better care of themselves, with coaches, therapists, personal doctors and diet plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We want to extend these interventions to the broad population, which will benefit most those with lower incomes who do not have the time, resources or wherewithal to do this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We hope everyone in Singapore will have such a friend, too – a family doctor to advise and nag us to do what is right for our long-term health and for our family.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We want to make it easier and affordable for everyone to stay healthy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will have a fuller debate on Healthier SG in the House later this year when we present the White Paper.

sections.label: Increase in registered doctors
sections.summary: Over five years, registered doctors with the Singapore Medical Council rose about 30%, from about 13,400 to 15,400.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In fact, over the last five years, the number of doctors has increased by about 30%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We are talking about registered doctors with the Singapore Medical Council – from about 13,400 to 15,400.

sections.label: Outcome-based KPIs and capitation
sections.summary: Moving to capitation requires outcome-based KPIs, including chronic illness prevalence, re-admission and clinical and cost effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Yes, we will have to measure the outcomes of success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier that we are moving to capitation and, along with the funding model, there will have to be a set of KPIs and these will have to be outcome-based.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I have mentioned some of them, such as prevalence of chronic illnesses, as well as the driving factors that lead to these outcomes, such as re-admission and various clinical effectiveness, cost effectiveness of treatments.

sections.label: GPs in primary care networks
sections.summary: GPs are encouraged to work together, with a third already in primary care networks, a starting point for Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As to the Member's second question whether GPs are encouraged to work together, the answer is yes, because a third of our GPs are now already in PCNs or primary care networks and that is a very important resource and very important starting point to bring them into Healthier SG.

sections.label: Preventive healthcare outcomes audit
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry will audit preventive healthcare efforts, noting chronic condition outcomes worsened as the proportion of older adults with three or more chronic conditions almost doubled between 2009 and 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But over the last 10 years, I think the outcomes for chronic conditions seem to have not done very well and perhaps, even gone in the opposite direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I noted in my Adjournment Motion speech on preventive healthcare that the proportion of older adults with three or more chronic conditions almost doubled between 2009 and 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I think the Minister and others have also elaborated on some data points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, my question is, will the Ministry reflect deeply and, perhaps, audit all the efforts that have gone into preventive healthcare in the last 10, 20 years to find out why there has been this disconnect between the investment and the efforts and the kind of outcomes that we have seen in the last 10 years of chronic conditions.

sections.label: Cleaners COVID-19 Healthcare Award eligibility
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State to confirm whether cleaners in healthcare institutions are eligible for the $4,000 COVID-19 Healthcare Award.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: It did not exactly say no, but it did not say yes and it said that there are other schemes for cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, I just wanted to confirm if I heard the Senior Minister of State correctly that now the position is that cleaners in healthcare institutions are eligible for this $4,000 COVID-19 Healthcare Award.

sections.label: COVID-19 Healthcare Award outsourced workers
sections.summary: The COVID-19 Healthcare Award was always intended for full-time outsourced workers in healthcare institutions, and an announcement on when and how much they get will follow shortly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for the COVID-19 Healthcare Award (CHA), the intention is and has always been, to also distribute to outsourced workers who are full-time, working in the healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It has always been the intention, but the details took a while draw up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And so, shortly after this, it will be announced and they will get to know when and how much they are getting.

sections.label: Doctor choice and consultation package
sections.summary: The answer is yes, choice of doctor will be preserved as a principle, and during consultation nothing will be prejudged, aiming for a compelling, attractive and affordable package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The short answer to the first question is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And I mentioned in my speech: there are residents who for various reasons, see a doctor that is not near their home and in fact, out of the cluster that they come under.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, choice will be preserved as a principle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second question: during our consultation, we will not prejudge what we want to include, or what we want to exclude.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I assure you it will not be the first time we hear that feedback and certainly will have to consider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We want a package that is compelling, attractive and that we can afford.

sections.label: Healthier people moderate healthcare costs
sections.summary: Making people healthier makes chronic diseases less likely, so healthcare costs can be moderated, though they will still increase due to ageing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: By making people healthier, it is less likely they will get chronic diseases and, so, healthcare costs can be moderated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It will still increase due to ageing, but we can moderate the increase.

sections.label: Responsibility for health and finances
sections.summary: Everyone is responsible for their own health and finances, and the help being given must be universal, not just for the middle class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are all responsible for our own health and in some sense, our own finances too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are helping, not just the middle class, but everyone else, it has to be universal.

sections.label: Outcome KPIs and life expectancy
sections.summary: The speaker says outcome KPIs have always existed and cites the highest life expectancy at birth for men and women across 204 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I mentioned about setting outcome KPIs, but they have always been there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I mentioned some of them, today we have the highest life expectancy at birth for men and women, across 204 countries.
